faq.q: How do I even apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank or broker using the ASBA (Applications Supported by Blocked Amount) facility. Your application money is blocked in your bank account and only debited if you are allotted shares.
A lot size is the minimum number of shares you must apply for in an IPO. You cannot apply for fewer than the specified lot size, and you must apply in multiples of it.

faq.q: What is the difference between Mainboard and SME IPOs?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger companies and list on the main exchanges (NSE, BSE). SME (Small and Medium Enterprises) IPOs are for smaller companies and list on dedicated SME platforms (like NSE Emerge or BSE SME) with slightly different regulations and typically smaller issue sizes.

faq.q: Can I apply for multiple lots?
faq.a: Yes, as a retail investor, you can apply for multiple lots, but your total application value cannot exceed ₹2 lakhs. If you wish to apply for more than ₹2 lakhs, you would fall under the HNI (High Net-worth Individual) category.

The cut-off price is the highest price within the price band. When you apply for an IPO, you can bid at a specific price or choose to bid at the "cut-off price," which means you are willing to pay whatever the final issue price is, provided it falls within the announced price band. This increases your chances of allotment in case the final price is fixed at the higher end of the band.
